For now, the integration supports [b]Standard chess[/b], allowing you to:[/p][list][*][p][b]Challenge your friends or other players[/b] from around the globe to real-time matches.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Play against Lichess's famous Stockfish AI[/b] at various difficulty levels.[/p][/*][*][p][b]View and continue all your ongoing Lichess games[/b]. Whether it's a rapid game or a correspondence match that lasts for weeks, you can pick up right where you left off.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Receive and manage challenges[/b] from other Lichess players.[/p][/*][*][p]Lichess Board API supports games with a base time of [b]10 minutes or longer[/b] (such as Rapid, Classical, and Correspondence chess).[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]All Lichess games are synchronized in real-time, and you can use in-game actions like offering draws and resigning, which are communicated directly with the Lichess server.[/p][p align="start"][b]How to get started:[/b][/p][olist][*][p]Update [b]Just Chess[/b] via Steam to the latest version.[/p][/*][*][p]Switch to the Lichess mode and press the new "Login" button.[/p][/*][*][p]Authorize the application on the browser page that opens.[/p][/*][*][p]You're all set! The main menu will now display your active Lichess games, and you can start creating new challenges.[/p][/*][/olist][p align="start"]This has been a massive development effort, and I'm proud to finally bring it to you.[/p][p][b]A Note on Pricing[/b][/p][p align="start"]This Lichess update marks a major milestone for [b]Just Chess[/b], and the value of the game has grown significantly. [/p][p align="start"]Thank you for your support![/p][list][*][p]The Just Chess Developer[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Next Steps: Lichess Integration
notes.notes: [p]Since the last update hasn’t produced new bug reports, I’ve started moving the development forward. The next big feature coming is [b]Lichess integration[/b].[/p][p]At first, the integration will only allow playing against the [b]Stockfish engine[/b], but challenging human players is also planned and will definitely be included later on. The first version will support the [b]standard game mode[/b] with basic functionality. The UI will allow you to create both untimed and timed games, and I aim to include the most common time controls. However, since the Lichess board API doesn’t seem to support the very fastest games, the minimum time control will be [b]10 minutes and upwards[/b].[/p][p]Early playtests are already underway. I can’t yet give an estimate for the release date, but so far things are progressing smoothly. I’m also aiming to design the UI features in a way that feels at least somewhat familiar to those who already use Lichess.[/p][p]Once the core features are in place, I will look into supporting other chess variants as well. Lichess has a very wide range of features, so I may not be able to implement absolutely everything — but the goal is to add real value to the game with this integration.[/p][p]Stay tuned, and thanks for playing![/p]

notes.title: Clock and Time Control Fixes
notes.notes:
We've deployed an update that addresses several important issues related to the game clock and official time controls, making timed games more accurate, fair, and intuitive.

1. Time Controls Now Add Time Correctly
We identified and fixed a critical bug in how multi-stage time controls (like FIDE's "90 minutes for 40 moves, then 30 minutes added") were handled. In some cases, the additional time was awarded one move too late.  We also corrected some underlying data values in the time control presets to ensure they match their descriptions.

2. Clock Display Improved for Clarity
We've also fixed an issue where the visual clock display could be misleading. Previously, if you gained time from increments and your total time went above the starting amount, the radial timer would appear "stuck" at 100%. With this update, the clock now intelligently treats your highest achieved time as the new "100%" mark. This means you will always see the clock visually ticking down during your turn, giving you a much more accurate sense of your time situation at a glance.

3. Consistent Time Bonus (Increment)
Finally, we fixed a logic error where the player's clock would behave differently from the AI's clock regarding increments. The time bonus is now applied consistently to both the player and the AI.

notes.title: Small Update: Self-Playing Chess Engine
notes.notes:
Just Chess has received a small but hopefully entertaining addition! With this update, the game can now play a match against itself. If the board is empty and the player has been inactive for a while, the engine will automatically start a self-play game where it controls both sides.

The self-play stops immediately if the player moves the mouse.

This update should not interfere with normal gameplay. Our hope is that this little feature adds a bit of liveliness and fun to the game when it's idle.

Thanks for playing Just Chess!

notes.title: 🧠 UCI Support, Revamped UI, and More Improvements!
notes.notes:
🧠 [b]UCI Support, Revamped UI, and More Improvements![/b]
This update introduces several major features, the most significant being:

🔌 [b]Support for UCI-Compatible Chess Engines[/b]
You can now use your own UCI-compatible chess engines instead of the built-in one! This allows you to play against powerful engines like Stockfish (tested with version 17), Komodo Dragon, and Gull directly within the game.

You can freely switch between the UCI engine and the internal engine any time before a chess match begins.

The toggle is located on the left side of the UI using the "UCI" and "Internal" buttons.

A new status indicator has been added to the UI to show whether the UCI engine loaded successfully. A green light means it was initialized correctly.

The internal engine is used by default.

The game remembers the last used UCI engine and attempts to launch it automatically next time.

Make sure to use a 64-bit version of your engine.

⚠️ [b]Only use engines downloaded from trusted sources.[/b] The developer is not responsible for any software you choose to run on your computer.

🎨 [b]Revamped User Interface[/b]
The interface has been reorganized to provide a smoother and more intuitive experience. Also, the game now remembers your last set audio volume and applies it automatically on launch.

♟ [b]Animated Piece Captures[/b]
Capturing a piece is now animated. When a piece is taken, it visibly moves off the board, making gameplay easier to follow and more visually engaging.

🧾 [b]PGN Improvements[/b]
You can now enter your own player name, which will appear in the PGN file.

The name can be changed freely as long as the game hasn't ended.

If you change your name, it will be updated in the PGN listing when the next move is made.

The engine name and difficulty level are now also stored in the PGN, in the format: Stockfish @875.

💸 [b]Upcoming Price Adjustment[/b]
This update introduces a major new feature (UCI engine support), and due to the added development work, the price of the game will increase slightly.

⚠️ [b]About This Update[/b]
This is a major update, and although I’ve tested it thoroughly, bugs may still occur. If you encounter any issues, your feedback is highly appreciated!

notes.title: 🔧 UCI engine support is in development – early testing underway!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! 👋

I'm currently working on adding UCI (Universal Chess Interface) support to Just Chess. This would allow players to use an external UCI-compatible chess engine (like Stockfish) instead of the built-in one.

This is still very much a work in progress — there’s a lot of testing and bug fixing ahead. I can't give a reliable estimate for when (or even if) the feature will be officially added, but I wanted to share that early testing is already underway.

Right now I’m testing with Stockfish 17, and focusing on making sure that existing game features (such as saving, move takebacks, difficulty setting, etc.) continue to work properly with a UCI engine. Some bugs have already shown up, but I’m working hard to sort them out and make everything as smooth as possible.

💡 Heads up: If the UCI support ends up being stable and gets officially added, it will likely increase the value of the game — and therefore its price. So if you’ve been thinking about getting Just Chess, now is a great time to grab it at the current price!

Thanks for your support!
